standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting an etale morphism from a closed subscheme to the ambient scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma allowing an etale morphism V -> Z from a closed subscheme to be lifted to an affine scheme U etale over X
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the lift U -> X to which the normal-scheme structure statement is applied.

standard_prerequisites.name: Separated etale morphisms over a normal scheme with separably closed function field
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma showing that on such a scheme a separated etale morphism is a disjoint union of open immersions
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the first statement, applied to U -> X.

core_obligations: Lift and apply the structure lemma (proof lines 14399-14404): the lifting lemma produces an affine U etale over X with V = U x_X Z, and the normal-scheme lemma applied to U -> X shows that U, hence V, is a finite disjoint union of open subschemes of Z.

Decompose the surjective finite case (proof lines 14406-14414): write V = coproduct of V_i with V_i -> Z an open immersion; since V -> Z is finite, each V_i -> Z is also closed, so the images U_i are both open and closed.

Build the section (proof lines 14415-14422): the displayed decomposition of Z into the open and closed strata indexed by the pairs (A, B) with A nonempty is disjoint because each point of Z lies in exactly one U_i-combination; each stratum is contained in a single U_i, so one gets a section of V -> Z.
proof_roadmap: Lift the etale cover of Z to an affine etale cover of X and apply the structure statement for normal schemes.
In the finite surjective case decompose the cover into open immersions and note they are simultaneously closed.
Use the open-and-closed decomposition of Z by the images to exhibit a section.
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes etale covers of a closed subscheme of an affine integral normal scheme with separably closed function field: they split into finitely many open subschemes, and a finite surjective one has a section (statement lines 14389-14396). The proof (proof lines 14398-14422) lifts the cover to an affine etale cover of the ambient scheme and applies the structure lemma for normal schemes, then decomposes the finite surjective case into open immersions that are simultaneously closed and reads off a section from the induced open-and-closed decomposition of Z. H2: one lift and one decomposition argument, written out.
